You can embed an R code chunk like this: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} data <- data.frame( id = 1:4, content = c("Item one", "Item two", "Ranged item", "Item four"), start = c("2016-01-10", "2016-01-11", "2016-01-20", "2016-02-14 15:00:00"), end = c(NA, NA, "2016-02-04", NA) ) timevis(data) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ``` timeline_1981_2009 <- data.frame( id = 1:10, content = c( "Event one", "Event two", "Event three", "Event four", "Event five", "Event six", "Event seven", "Event eight", "Event nine", "Event ten" ), start = c( "1981-01-01", "1984-01-01", "1987-01-01", "1991-01-01", "1994-01-01", "1997-01-01", "2001-01-01", "2004-01-01", "2007-01-01", "2009-01-01" ), end = c( NA, NA, NA, "1993-12-31", NA, NA, "2003-12-31", NA, NA, NA ), stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) timevis(timeline_1981_2009) ``` Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
